newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen extending profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen extending profit-taking.

text.p: Polish shares fell in profit -taking for the second day in a row in stable volume and analysts braced for more losses saying fears of a U.S. rate rise and labour protests in Poland were also dampening demand.
The main market's WIG index fell 2.3 percent, to 16,087.5, and trade was stable at 134.4 million zlotys ($44.7 million) on all three markets as 66 issues fell, 12 rose and 14 were flat.

"Gains of some stocks in continuous trade show there might be a rebound on Friday, but if so it could be used for more selling as investors fear the March 25 Fed meeting," said Tomasz Cwintal of BGZ brokerage.
Some analysts said the 10-percent slide from last week was caused mainly by retail players taking profits after a 30-percent surge since early 1997.
Some said recent protests in defence of the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard were additionally cooling down small investor mood.
They said large players kept on the sidelines waiting for better bargains and could step in and start buying when the bourse slips to about 15,500.

Analysts were optimistic in the longer term saying Poland's economy looked sound and with Finance Minister predicting inflation this month possibly below 17 percent year-on-year, the Warsaw market remained a good long-term investment.

Construction firm Espebepe plunged 28.4 percent on mounting concern that the firm would go bankrupt, after the bourse allowed it to trade without the regular daily 10-percent price fluctuation limit on Thursday.
In the continuous trade most stocks rose and the WIG 20 index closed at 1,624.2 points, 1.7 percent higher than at the regular session.
